---
title: "simstim agents login"
---

<!-- Generated by `just docs` from the code. Do not edit by hand. -->

Start an agent's own login on a host, in a session you can answer.

```text
simstim agents login <agent> [<host>] [flags]
```

Starts the agent's own login, such as `claude auth login`, in a session named `login-<agent>` on the host, and attaches to it. When that login already runs, it attaches to it instead. When you leave, it checks the login again. The login runs again also when the agent is logged in, for example to change the account. The agent keeps its login on the host. simstim never sees it.

## Examples

```sh
simstim agents login claude my-vps
simstim agents login claude my-vps --json   # start it, and print the session
```

## Flags

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--host <string>` | the host, as the second argument names it |
| `--json` | print JSON for scripts, and ask nothing (see docs/how-to/scripting.md) |

## Flags from the parent command

| Flag | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `--debug[=<categories>]` | turn on the debug mode, with every category, or with the categories listed: attach, net, memory, launcher, runtime. A list binds only in the = form, such as `--debug=net` |
| `--debug-file <file>` | write the client's debug records to this file. On its own, it turns on every category (SIMSTIM_DEBUG_FILE does the same) |
| `--no-color` | print no colour (NO_COLOR does the same) |
| `--no-input` | ask nothing: a question that needs an answer fails with exit code 4, and names the flag that answers it (SIMSTIM_NO_INPUT=1 does the same) |

Part of [`agents`](agents.md): list the agents, install one on a host, and log in to it.
